overall: Checker is clean (228/228 items, all 73 tokens covered) and most items are true, school-level and well outside the concept. The main recurring problem is forced wording for case-sensitive tokens: words capitalized or quoted mid-sentence only to get the token (Grin, Road Hog, Hogtied, Quirky, Umbrage, Riddle, Inquisitorial, Potter's wheel/field, Rowing/Rowdy/Rowland, quoted Harry names, "warts", "wizard" Prospero); for no-space tokens, starting the question with the word is natural and tokenizes correctly (verified for Harry Lime, Hogs, Hogtied, Potter's, Rowing, Rowdy, Rowland). Second, several items give a non-token clue that fully determines the answer (Mrs Dalloway, General Theory, Diaz/Barrymore, J.R. Ewing, Allan Quatermain, earldom, news anchor -> Anchorman). Neutrality: both Hermione tokens should become exclusive (Winter's Tale origin is fan trivia; the Greek uses are obscure), and the Draco=dragon and Bloomsbury=London items lean on facts fans know from the concept; Umbrage is a concept pun. Smaller issues: an ambiguous distractor (Mustang is Merlin-powered), giveaway distractors (Mycroft among surnames), weak distractors (owls, D&D spellbook), a few items too obscure for a 2B model (driblet, Cedric the Entertainer, McGoohan, potter wasp), and paraphrase pairs (Granger 3/4, wiz 1/4).
